title: RANDOMIZE
author: jack
description: One-press randomizers on two pages, same four controls left to right: SCL (scale for PIT), UNDO (turn left = undo, turn right = redo through the last 8 RND/PIT presses; FUNC + press = undo), RND (0-100 % of the pattern length; press scatters that many trigs; a new trig takes the note remembered for its step), PIT (0-36 semitones; press gives every step, trig or not, a new note within +/-PIT of the TRIG page ROOT; with a scale, root/fifth/third come up more often and chords stay in key). MIDI tracks: MIDI Source page (SYN1), bottom row. Synth tracks: Amplitude page 2/2, top row. 0 = a press does nothing. A spring reset switch (the LFO.T toggle; MIDI Source page PROG slot, synth Amplitude page 1 empty slot): a firm turn right resets this track's randomizer and wipes its trigs, then it springs back. MIDI tracks also get LEN+ (the SBNK slot, above RND): 0-100 % of the trigs get a random longer length, anywhere up to 4 steps above the original, on a press (never shorter, always from the original length; undoable). At 0 % a LEN+ press puts every length it changed back to the original.
